nina: FYI: rolling out two small but cross-cutting SDK/docs changes today. Goal is better example discovery and fewer stale snippets in repos. No breaking runtime changes.

oscar: quick bullets?

nina: 1) docs-local: `redwood docs serve --watch` CLI (dev preview) so engineers can preview snippet linting locally. 2) examples auto-update policy: well allow a docs job to open PRs that update example snippets in our public example repos when lint fixes are trivial (formatting, schema labels). 3) deprecating HTML-embedded snippets in docs pages (we prefer fenced code blocks for parsing).

cli-bot: install: pipx install redwood-docs-cli@preview or npm i -g @redwood/docs-cli@preview 

lena: Nice. For the auto-PRs, what's considered "trivial"?

nina: Trivial = single-file snippet label add, whitespace/formatting changes, or schema tag correction. Anything that changes logic or network calls will be skipped and flagged for manual review. Auto-PRs will be limited to one per repo per 24h to avoid noise.

support: Heads-up: well need a canned reply explaining why examples changed automatically for customers who pin example repos.

qa: Will docs-lint run on these auto-PRs? possible flakiness?

nina: Yes, auto-PRs are generated after docs-lint passes locally; CI still runs and may block merge. We added a short grace period: if CI blocks the auto-PR due to unrelated flakiness, the job will retry once and then open a manual-ticket instead of hammering.

oscar: Telemetry? can we count how many examples are updated automatically?

nina: Yes  metric: docs.auto_prs.count and docs.local.serves.count. Also tag PRs with `[docs-auto]` and include a short changelog in the PR body.

cli-bot: preview deploy of docs tools done (deploy-2026-03-24-02) :white_check_mark:

lena: HTML snippet removal: timeline?

nina: Timeline: immediate - new docs authoring should avoid HTML-embedded snippets; 30 days - docs-lint flags HTML snippets as warnings; 60 days - treat them as errors in new PRs; 90 days - we will convert trivial cases in the background and open auto-PRs for the rest. We'll publish a migration helper for authors.

support: Thanks. I'll draft customer-facing blurb: "We're improving how examples are maintained so they stay correct and searchable. Small non-destructive changes may be proposed to example repos to keep snippets current."

qa: One risk: auto-PRs changing formatting may upset example backport pipelines. Can we opt-out per-repo?

nina: Yes, we added an opt-out file `.docs-auto-prs-ignore` at repo root. If present, auto-PRs won't be opened. We'll document that in the guide.

oscar: Action items?

nina: - docs: publish CLI guide + migrate note (lena)
- eng: monitor docs.auto_prs.* metrics (oscar)
- support: KB blurb and canned replies (support)
- qa: spot-check conversions and report false positives (qa)

cli-bot: note: this thread will be pinned to #announcements for 48h

nina: Thanks all. Low risk rollout, but please flag noisy auto-PRs or lint false positives in this thread. :seedling:
